subject: physics
title: Measurements & Uncertainties Adventure 3: Propagating uncertainties
meta_desc: Physics — absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation rules, error in derived quantities.
final_note: You learned add absolute uncertainties when summing, add % uncertainties when multiplying or dividing, multiply % by power for exponents.

concepts.def: Δx in same units as x

walkthroughs.body_html:
For y = a + b or y = a − b: Δy = Δa + Δb (add absolutes).

For y = a × b or y = a/b: Δy/y = Δa/a + Δb/b (add fractionals/percentages).

For y = aⁿ: Δy/y = n × Δa/a.

On graphs, error bars show Δ for each axis.

Draw best-fit line, then max-gradient and min-gradient lines that still pass through error bars.

Slope uncertainty = (m_max − m_min) / 2.

This is the gold-standard for IA Physics — examiners look for it.

What property of a sound wave determines its pitch?
options: There is no field around a positive charge unless another charge is present.
Amplitude determines pitch — a bigger wave is a higher-pitched note.
The frequency — higher frequency means higher pitch.
The speed of the wave determines pitch — faster waves sound higher.

mcqs.q: In which direction does an electric field point near a positive charge?
options: Radially inwards because positive attracts negative.
There is no field around a positive charge unless another charge is present.
Wider spacing means a stronger field because the lines have more room to act.
Radially outwards — the field is defined by the force on a positive test charge, which is repelled.

mcqs.q: What does the spacing of field lines on a diagram indicate?
options: There is no field around a positive charge unless another charge is present.
Wider spacing means a stronger field because the lines have more room to act.
Field lines are equally important regardless of spacing — only the arrows matter.
The strength of the field — closer lines mean a stronger field.
